AWARD 1.

Vide this order I shall dispose off the 'Detailed Accident Report' (hereinafter referred to as 'DAR')
filed by the police with regard to the accident occurred on 26.06.2021 in which injured Baby Ji Dubey (hereinafter referred to as 'petitioner') suffered injuries.
DAR was treated as claim petition under Section 166 (4) of M.V. Act.

Copy of DAR was supplied the petitioner as well as to Sahrukh Khan (hereinafter referred to as 'respondent no. 1'), Akbar Khan (hereinafter referred to as 'respondent no. 2') and Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as 'respondent no. 3') i.e.
driver, owner and insurance company of vehicle involved in the accident i.e. motorcycle bearing registration no. HR55AK 2093 (hereinafter referred to as 'vehicle in question').

2. In brief, the facts of the case are that during the investigation, the Investigating Officer has recorded the statement of injured Babu Ji Dubey, which is reproduced us under:-
"On 26/06/21 at around 6.15 PM in the evening, I along with my cousin Pawan S/o Kanhaiya went to Shed No. 11 fruits Mandi Azadpur Delhi Shri Vinayak I had come to fruits Shop No. A 1060 to offer mangoes to him.
I was standing at Shed No. 11 Shri Vinayak Fruits, Pawan was also standing near me.
At this time, the driver of truck No. HR 55 AK-2093 TATA 1512 reversed his truck very fast and carelessly without turning on the horn and lights.
The rear axle of which was open and I got injured near the ankle of my right leg and other parts of the body and my leg started bleeding.
When I shouted, the driver of truck No. HR 55 MACT no. 40/23 SUNIL KUMAR Babu Ji Dubey Vs. Sahrukh Khan & Ors.

Onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioner and to prove the same, petitioner examined himself as PW1.
Petitioner as PW1 has deposed that on 26.06.2021 he along with his cousin Pawan came at Fruits, Shop No. 1060, Shed No.11, Azadpur Fruit Mandi to load Mangoes on truck.

He was standing near Sh.

His cousin Pawan also standing with him.
At that time, the truck driver of vehicle bearing No. HR 55 AK 2093 TATA 1512 (vehicle in question) in rash and negligent manner without horn, without light indication drove backward his truck.
The dalla of the offending vehicle was opened and the said daala fell on the ankle of his right foot, due to which he sustained grievous injury and some injury on other parts of his body.

When he shouted, the driver of the offending vehicle bearing no. HR 55 AK 2093 drove his vehicle forward and parked the same near the Shed No.11 and the driver of the said vehicle ran away from the spot.
His cousin brother Pawan put him on hathrehari (hand cart) and took him to BJRM Hospital, Jahangir Puri, Delhi from where he was referred to Safderjung Hospital for treatment.
Petitioner / PW1 has not at all been cross examined by respondents no. 1 & 2.

Further, the DAR collectively Ex. PW1/6 shows that respondent no.1 was charge sheeted by the police for offences punishable under Section 279/338 IPC.
Apart from deposition of PW1, the fact that petitioner suffered injuries in the accident is also supported by his medical documents MLC etc. filed along with the DAR collectively Ex. PW1/6.
Respondent no. 1 has not placed on record any document to disprove the factum of rash and negligent driving by him.
Further, there is nothing on record which shows that respondent no. 1 has ever approached to any higher authority against false his implication in the present case.

Relying upon judgment in Pushpabai Purshottam Udeshi & Ors vs Ranjit Ginning & Pressing Co.

sentences.text: "The general purport of the words res ipsa loquitur is that the accident "speaks for itself" or tell's its own story.
There are cases in which the accident speaks for itself so that it is sufficient for the plaintiff to prove the accident and nothing more.
It will then be for the defendant to establish that the accident happened due to some other cause than his own negligence.

Salmond on the Law of Torts (15th Ed.) at p. 306 Babu Ji Dubey vs Sharukh Khan on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51089925/
5 states: "The maxim res ipsa loquitur applies whenever it is so improbable that such an accident would have happened without the negligence of the defendant that a reasonable jury could find without further evidence that it was so caused."

sentences.text: In Halsbury's Laws of England, 3rd Ed., Vol. 28, at p. 77, the position is stated thus: "An exception to the general rule that the burden of proof of the alleged negligence is in the first instance on the plaintiff occurs wherever the facts already established are such that .the proper and natural inference arising from them is ,that the injury complained of was caused by the defendant's negligence, or where the event charged as negligence "tells its own story' of negligence on the part of the defendant, the story so told being clear and unambiguous."

Further, relying upon the judgment of Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs. Phulwant Mahendra Singh,
Miscellaneous Appeal no.239/1992 decided by Hon'ble Madhya Pradesh High Court on 29.07.1993 in which it is held as under: -

Considering all this, it stands proved that accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1 and petitioner suffered grievous injuries in the said accident

Accordingly, the question of right of the injured for claiming of compensation is decided in favour of the petitioner.

Medical bills proved and placed on record are of Rs. 58,375/- and during the arguments,
Ld. Counsel for petitioner stated at Bar that petitioner was having no mediclaim policy and above sated amount of medical bills has not been got reimbursed from any authority.
Accordingly, this amount of Rs. 58,375/- is awarded to the petitioner towards medical expenditure.

Though, except deposition of petitioner, there is no evidence to verify that petitioner has spent any amount on special diet and no witness has been examined for proving the conveyance expenditure etc.

However, keeping in view the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and his long treatment record, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner must have incurred expenses on special diet required for his speedy recovery as well as on travel to hospitals etc.
Accordingly, Rs.20,000/- each towards special diet and conveyance.

11. It is a matter of record that a disability certificate issued by the Department of Empowerment of persons with Disabilities, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India Ex.
PW1/3 placed and proved on record as per which the petitioner is a case of locomotor disability and has suffered 40% permanent disability in relation to his right foot.

12. As far as loss of income during the treatment and loss of income on account of loss of future earning due to disability is concerned, through petitioner as PW1 deposed that he was earning Rs.
30,000-40,000/- per month but admittedly there is no document to prove the contention except deposition of petitioner.
Hence, the income of petitioner could not be proved on record and no document with regard to education qualification of petitioner has been filed on record.

sentences.text: Furthermore, as per DAR filed by the IO, the petitioner was residing at Shop No. D196, Azadpur Sabji Mandi, Delhi at that time.
Hence, contention of respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. is not tenable in this regard and rejected.

In such scenario, to calculate the extent of compensation with respect to his loss of income during the period of treatment and loss to future earning, the minimum wages of unskilled labour, at that prevalent time has to be taken, which was Rs.15,908/-, in Delhi and same is taken for purpose of calculating the loss of income during treatment and future loss of income.
13. Considering the testimony of PW1 and long treatment record of petitioner, it is presumed that petitioner could not continue his work during his treatment i.e. about 6 months.

Accordingly, a sum of Rs. 95,448/- (15,908x6) for loss of income during the period of his treatment for 6 months and during this period he must have taken the services of an attendant and hence a sum of Rs.30,000/-
(5000x6) for 6 months, towards attendant charges are awarded to the petitioner.

14. As per Ex. PW1/1 i.e. Aadhar card of petitioner, his date of birth is 01.01.1994, which inter alias means that petitioner was 27 years and 5 months in age at the time of accident and as stated above,
petitioner suffered 40% permanent disability, no doubt, this kind of disability would hamper his day to day activity and work for gain.
Hence, his functional disability / percentage of loss of earning capacity in relation to disability is taken as 20% qua whole body.

A multiplier of 17 (as per the judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Sarla Verma vs Delhi Transport Corporation, 2009 ACJ 1298) is taken for calculating his loss to future earnings.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Relying upon judgment in Pushpabai Purshottam Udeshi & Ors vs Ranjit Ginning & Pressing Co.
(P) Ltd. & Anr. 1977 (2) SCC 745 Civil Appeal No. 2071 of 1968, decided on March 25,
1977 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India wherein it was held as under: -
The general purport of the words res ipsa loquitur is that the accident speaks for itself or tells its own story".
Thus, Claims Tribunal while dealing with the law of torts in motor accident cases applies the principle of "res ipsa loquitur".
Considering all this, it stands proved that accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1 and petitioner suffered grievous injuries in the said accident
Accordingly, the question of right of the injured for claiming of compensation is decided in favour of the petitioner.
12. As far as loss of income during the treatment and loss of income on account of loss of future earning due to disability is concerned, through petitioner as PW1 deposed that he was earning Rs.
30,000-40,000/- per month but admittedly there is no document to prove the contention except deposition of petitioner.
Hence, the income of petitioner could not be proved on record and no document with regard to education qualification of petitioner has been filed on record.
13. Considering the testimony of PW1 and long treatment record of petitioner, it is presumed that petitioner could not continue his work during his treatment i.e. about 6 months.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs. 95,448/- (15,908x6) for loss of income during the period of his treatment for 6 months and during this period he must have taken the services of an attendant and hence a sum of Rs.30,000/-
(5000x6) for 6 months, towards attendant charges are awarded to the petitioner.
Hence, his functional disability / percentage of loss of earning capacity in relation to disability is taken as 20% qua whole body.
Further, as per the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, of Hon'ble Supreme Court, petitioner is also entitled to get 40% of enhancement of salary, as he was below 40 years in age SUNIL by SUNIL KUMAR Date: 2025.05.06 Page no. 9 16:03:36 +0530 Babu Ji Dubey Vs. Sahrukh Khan & Ors.
at the time of accident.

6,49,046.4, is allowed to petitioner, as loss of future earnings, due to permanent disability.
No tax is deducted since the said income of petitioner is not taxable.
